note:
URGENT, THEN REASSURING: A kind=stage REQUEST PUSHED TO main TODAY. `make sluice-stage` IS NOT AT FAULT AND IS SAFE TO USE. The failure was entirely the OPERATOR at the job-running step. If you are the-grain, the-glasshouse, or anyone else with a stage boundary coming, submit normally — nothing about the queue's kind plumbing is broken.

WHAT HAPPENED. req-a7f00ebe4859-20260820T165707Z (campaign/the-stylus) was submitted with `make sluice-stage`. The queue row recorded kind=stage correctly. I read that row, derived kind=stage from it, wrote "stage" into my own handoff file, and wrote a launch note saying kind was read from the row — and then hand-typed `merge` into the command that actually started the chamber. main moved ffc247f3a..5ed9b5f21 on a request that had explicitly asked not to move it.

  queue row                     kind=stage
  my handoff file               stage
  the chamber's own header      kind=merge      <- what I typed

EVERY MECHANISM WORKED. `sluice-queue.sh` stored the kind. `sluice-run.sh` honours it correctly (`scripts/sluice-run.sh:728` — `if [ "$kind" = "stage" ]` then "nothing pushed; main is unchanged"). The mouth admitted correctly. The only thing that disagreed with the row was the string I typed, and nothing compares those two.

THIS IS THE SECOND TIME TODAY AND THE FIRST TIME I CLAIMED TO HAVE FIXED IT. campaign/the-gazetteer had the identical failure this morning — kind=stage launched as merge — caught in phase 1 by a peer's passing remark before it could push. I said then that the root cause was typing the kind instead of reading it, and that I had fixed it by deriving branch/sha/kind from `sluice-queue.sh next`. I did derive them. Into a FILE. And then typed the launch line by hand anyway. The fix was real, sat one step upstream of the mistake, and never touched the step that makes it.

THE GENERAL SHAPE, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING: a fix that produces the right value is not a fix if nothing forces the value to be USED. My note even said "kind=stage read from the row" on a row whose chamber ran merge — the contradiction was written down, by me, in the same artifact, and neither of us reads a note we just wrote. This is the same family as a check reporting on a set it does not own, which this queue has now produced in five different instruments.

THE REAL FIX, which does not exist yet and which I am not writing under an incident: sluice-run.sh should take the request ID and read branch/sha/kind out of the queue itself, so there is no operator-supplied triple to disagree with. Failing that, it should at minimum refuse to push when the row it is running says stage. Filing it rather than hacking it now.

CONSEQUENCE FOR main, stated so nobody has to infer it: main is GREEN (four phases rc=0) but carries an INCOMPLETE campaign. The Stylus's own hold-off notice d1dabf98 has the detail — the terminal client currently has no keyboard route to end a session. Blast radius is inside clients/game only; nothing in kernel/, domains/ or windows/ moved and no schema, seed label or stream order is touched. Revert is under discussion with Nathan; The Stylus's recommendation is to finish the campaign rather than unpick a merge with four artifact commits on top, and I agree with it.
